bluf: Kepler Group is a New York growth marketing agency owned by kyu collective, founded in 2012 with 600+ people, selling media, commerce, analytics and consulting run through its proprietary Kip platform. It is doing measurement led media with an AI search edge: Kip AIR for AI brand discovery, and since 2026-05 the inaugural agency partner in Pacvue's ChatGPT ads pilot. Where it is going: ads inside assistants, with holdout measurement. The thing a rival should know: 0 of 2 house tests pass, no llms.txt while selling AI visibility and nothing updated in its sitemap for 12 months, and 8 of 9 clients are names only.
doing:
Kepler positions itself as a global growth marketing agency fusing advanced analytics, human insight and creativity, run through its proprietary Kepler Intelligence Platform, Kip. In plain words: a measurement first media agency for enterprise brands that sells its own platform as the reason to buy the media through it. Its headline claim is that it was presented as Google's #1 partner for brand awareness at the 2023 Google Premier Partner Awards, quoted as its claim.

The sold mix has one lead line, data and measurement (scored 3: the homepage meta leads with data analytics, Kip won a MarTech Best Marketing Performance Management Solution award, MMM and Meta incrementality work for easyJet). Three lines score 2 and sit in the core: AI search (Kip AIR for AI brand discovery on the homepage, a GEO guide, Pacvue's first agency partner for ChatGPT ads), programmatic and CTV (DSP and CTV and OTT expertise pages, an iFly streaming TV and Prime Video case, an AdExchanger Best Commerce Media Technology award) and retail media (Commerce and Amazon service lines, a Hasbro holiday case across Amazon and Walmart, a retail media networks guide). Paid search and paid social score only 1 each, so the Horus read treats paid media as not a core line. Services listed: media and CRM, consulting, commerce, Amazon, technology and AI, B2B, analytics, creative. Proprietary: Kip and Kip AIR. Partners: Google Premier Partner and Pacvue.

AI posture: Kip and Kip AIR for shaping AI driven brand discovery, plus early activation of ChatGPT ads through Pacvue. Moves: 2026-05, named Pacvue's inaugural independent agency partner for its ChatGPT ads pilot, activating 10+ brands; undated, joined forces with Infectious Media to form one global offering. Pricing signals: none. Conspicuously absent for a media agency of its kind: any SEO, content or creator line (each scored 0), a live blog, and an llms.txt on a site selling AI visibility.
clients:
The record types the client as enterprise, across pharma, apparel and sportswear, toys and games, travel and airlines, media and entertainment, delivery and marketplaces, retail and jewelry, and consumer appliances. The home market is the US, New York headquartered, with offices in Philadelphia, Chicago, San Francisco, San Jose, Toronto, Ottawa, London, Tokyo, Singapore and Manila.

The needs read lists 9 clients, 1 observed and 8 named only, from 3 case studies and 6 slugs. Hasbro is the observed one: a case titled with Kepler creative, coded brand and creative, so the mix is that single code (share 1.0); the capability note adds that the Hasbro holiday case ran across Amazon and Walmart, a retail media need observed only as a note. The other 8 are names only: iFly, easyJet, Fila, Bloomberg, DoorDash, Ross-Simons, Versuni and F1 Las Vegas, with needs inferred from what the agency leads with, measurement and media. The capability notes hint at two: easyJet under MMM and Meta incrementality (data and measurement) and iFly under streaming TV and Prime Video (programmatic and CTV). No client sits on another tracked agency's book, so nothing here is shared.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places Kepler best for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better), both driven by data and measurement, and most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out). It is likely, with moderate confidence, that these enterprise brands buy the measurement and the assistant ad tests and let the platforms take the buying hours, which fits what Kepler sells.
house:
Say and do: 0 of 2 tested lines are practised on its own house. AI search is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt, with only 3 AI topic URLs in its sitemap. Publishing cadence is contradicted: a blog exists but nothing has been updated in the sitemap for 12 months, the sitemap listing 162 URLs with 0 updated in 90 days and 0 in 365. Those two are the flagged gaps. No AI crawlers are blocked. Google: it runs 3 text ads of its own in the Transparency Center, all 3 in the last 30 days, under the advertiser name Kepler, last shown 2026-09-27; no sample copy was captured. LinkedIn: none, 0 ads match the name query, for an agency with a B2B service line.

The site is Framer with GTM, GA4 and a LinkedIn Insight pixel, the only social pixel; no testing tools and no ABM stack were detected. Meta and TikTok status is not recorded.
market:
The Horus read scores Kepler at a tailwind index of 19.1, band Favored, 69th percentile, say and do integrity 0. Best placed for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net 0.375, data and measurement at +2) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better, net 0.375). Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out, net -0.53). Best fit is The Walled Oasis at 46/100. Moves: making P8 (assistant ads tested with holdouts), partial on P1 (AI visibility sold, not audited), P2 and P7, unknown on P5, absent on P6, P3 and P4 not applicable.

The Monsoon read: index 46.7, band Breeze; migration 60.2 against displacement 33.2, with a holdco term of 10 and an observed hub office term of 12. The verdict puts 38 of the index on the sold mix, data and measurement (10) and AI search (7), and the delivery footprint is observed: San Jose and Manila are listed as hub offices, with the shore split at 62% South and Southeast Asia and 31% Latin America. No onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the house against the platform pitch. Kepler sells AI brand discovery through Kip AIR and publishes no llms.txt, and it sells analytics led media while its own blog has had nothing updated in 12 months. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival with an audited citation share product and a live publishing cadence wins the AI discovery line at the enterprise brands it names (Hasbro, easyJet, DoorDash). Falsifier: Kepler publishing llms.txt and a Kip AIR scorecard with citation share for a named client.

Second, no public pricing model, so an outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot hold in public; the Monsoon displacement of 33.2 says this book does not buy on price, so the offer must be outcome, not rate. Third, 8 of 9 clients are names only, a question for those buyers. Fourth, KJ6: the hollowing removes the analyst hours behind Kip. The caution is P8: Kepler already tests assistant ads with holdouts through Pacvue, so a rival is unlikely to beat it there and should compete on feeds, entities and the machine readable product data those assistants consume, where its P2 move is only partial.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco sets a reference for a kyu collective agency with no public price and sharpens its KJ6 exposure.

I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, next reading December 2026 to January 2027: disclosed AI checkout GMV strengthens KJ4, its first tailwind, and the retail media line, while high Shopify opt out rates would slow both.
The dated move to follow is the 2026-05 Pacvue ChatGPT ads pilot with 10+ brands activated: a published result with holdouts would make its P8 lead concrete and price the channel for everyone else.
The undated Infectious Media combination: a date and a visible global offering would change the office and delivery read.

The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile, and a sitemap still idle after 12 months would confirm the publishing contradiction.
